title: Canonical derived coefficient normalization arrows
statement: Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on an essentially small category $C$, with $C$ in object universe $u+1$ and morphism universe $u$, and let $q:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings in universe $u+1$. Use sheaves of fixed-coefficient modules as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with the same construction on any such site, and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $c_{J,R}:D(R)\to D(J,R)$ for the termwise exact constant-sheaf functor [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $U_q:D(S)\to D(R)$ for termwise restriction of scalars, and $U_{J,q}:D(J,S)\to D(J,R)$ for termwise sheaf coefficient restriction. The constant module sheaf functor and both restriction functors are additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits; coefficient restriction commutes with sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Their derived functors are the localizations of those exact functors. The canonical comparison $\gamma:c_{J,S}U_{J,q}\simeq U_qc_{J,R}$ (composition written in application order) is obtained by localizing the constant-sheaf/restriction-of-scalars comparison. For $M\in D(R)$, $N\in D(S)$ and $d:M\to U_qN$, define its constant normalization arrow to be $c_{J,R}(d)$ followed by $\gamma_N^{-1}$, from $c_{J,R}M$ to $U_{J,q}c_{J,S}N$. A specified derived scalar-extension isomorphism $M\otimes_R^LS\simeq N$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is equivalently encoded by this specified $d$ and initiality [def-galois-initial-mono] of $(N,d)$ in the structured-arrow category $(M\downarrow U_q)$; use the existing universal-arrow notion, not a new predicate. The same encoding applies to sheaves. For any continuous functor $F:C\to D$ between sites [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] of these sizes, define the canonical transformation $U_{J,q}F_R^*\to F_S^*U_{K,q}$ as the mate of the identity square expressing commutation of sectionwise direct image with restriction of coefficients, using the canonical sheafified-presheaf inverse-image adjunction. This mate is an isomorphism, since restriction commutes with all colimits and sheafification; its inverse is the unique inverse of that mate. No extra exactness of $F^*$ is assumed for this underived comparison.

proof.text: For normalizationCoefficientExactness, apply the existing finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation instances for constantSheaf. Restriction of scalars is both a left adjoint (to coextension) and a right adjoint (to extension). Lift restriction/coextension to sheaves with sheafComposeAdjunction. The standard adjoint preservation instances give exactness, sheafCompose_additive gives additivity, and the Sites.Adjunction instance gives preservation of sheafification. These are direct applications of the existing Mathlib and source-library APIs.

For normalizationModuleRestrictExactness, use ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj and ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj in the fixed coefficient universe. Additivity is the existing restriction-of-scalars instance, and both finite preservation assertions follow from these two adjunctions.

For normalizationPullbackMate_isIso, restriction/coextension gives adjunctions adjJ and adjK on the two sheaf categories. Sectionwise direct image commutes definitionally with coextension, giving an identity square gamma between right adjoints. Its inverse mate along adjK and adjJ is the identity restriction/direct-image square: on every section this is precisely the left triangle identity for restriction/coextension. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies the specified inverse-image mate with the conjugate of gamma for the two composite adjunctions. Apply conjugateEquiv_symm_iso to the identity natural transformation. This is an application of the existing mates API, with the sectionwise triangle identity as the only component calculation.
